brief:
In Gaza, death comes not only from bombardment but from waiting for improvements that never arrive and from deteriorating tent shelters before rains begin, according to Shehab Wire. The situation reflects widespread international silence paired with minimal action on the ground.

The report raises fundamental questions about responsibility for providing adequate housing to displaced Palestinians, framing shelter as a humanitarian obligation rather than charity or conditional aid.

title: Gaza displacement crisis demands dignified shelter as human right
